HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. MANGA ACTION, hard DUTCH, medium close on the parapet. ONE DEVICE: the straight ring-pommel sword as a hard steel line across the Goguryeo king’s throat. LEFT face of the sheet = King Geunchogo: FACE AND GARMENTS from /ch_gunchogo.png — square Korean face, full dark beard, vermilion-red court po, gold dragon shoulders, black silk cap with twin gold flame ornaments. He is mid-stroke, mouth set, a little cruel, not a standing portrait. The Goguryeo king is a DIFFERENT older man — grey at the temples, red Goguryeo court silk and steel lamellar, peaked helm knocked back — NEVER clone Geunchogo’s face onto him. Extreme foreshortening: the blade comes across the lens. Blood as a thin dark ribbon on frozen stone, not a gore catalog. Keep Pyongyang’s red two-tier munru and stone walls from the place board in bokeh. IGNORE any curved sword on any portrait. The weapon is the attached sw_bidam board: small iron ring pommel at the heel of the fist, short grip, thin metal band, NO hand guard, perfectly STRAIGHT narrow blade. #eec052 as cold morning on Geunchogo’s gold ornaments. Day ground, storm-pale. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. No text. No watermark. MANGA ACTION FRAME in the character-intro-card painted look, NOT a calm posed still: a single seinen historical-manga action panel — bold dry-brush sumi-ink SPEED LINES streaking along the motion, radial FOCUS LINES converging on the FACE, motion smears on hair, cloth, limbs, mane and dirt, flung ink-splatter, extreme foreshortening and a hard dutch tilt so the frame itself feels like it is moving. FACES are LARGE and acting — shout, snarl, grin, grit, terror, determination — never a calm fashion plate, never the back of a head as the subject. Full-bleed: NO panel borders, NO speech bubbles, NO onomatopoeia or sound-effect lettering, NO text of any kind. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = gyeonggeunchogo. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_pyongyang_fortress (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). BOTTOM ROW: the only sword design. KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. KING GUNCHOGO — Look: Baekje’s thirteenth king in his prime: square Korean face, heavy brows, a full dark beard, unhurried slightly cruel eyes. Dress: Vermilion-red court po with gold dragon shoulder-plates, white inner collar, dark sash, black silk cap with twin openwork gold flame ornaments (attached /ch_gunchogo.png). Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. Colour #eec052. PLACE Pyongyang (평양성) — attached board /pl_pyongyang_fortress.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Pyongyang: Goguryeo walled city on the Taedong, stone walls and red munru gate pavilions. Any sword is the ancient straight Korean ring-pommel dao: a small iron ring pommel, a short wrapped grip, a thin metal band and NO hand guard, a perfectly straight blade — never a katana, never a tsuba. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
